name: Turkish get-up
pattern: Slow full-body sequence from lying to standing and back, one arm holding a weight straight up the whole time.
setup: Lie on your back, weight in your right hand, arm straight up over your shoulder.
Right knee bent, foot flat; left leg straight and out at about 45°, left arm out at 45°.
Wrist straight, eyes on the weight.

steps.text: Press the weight up and roll onto your left elbow, pushing with your right foot.
Push up from the elbow to your left hand; sit tall with the chest open.
Squeeze your glutes and lift your hips into a straight line.
Swing your left leg under you to kneel on the left knee.
Lift your hand off the floor, line up the back shin and come to a tall kneel.
Step up like a lunge to standing, weight still straight overhead. Then reverse every step.

cues.cue: Weight arm locked and vertical at every stage.
cues.why: The shoulder muscles work to hold the arm stable; a bent or drifting arm loses that and risks the shoulder.

cues.cue: Watch the weight until you kneel.
cues.why: It keeps the arm over the shoulder while the body moves under it.

cues.cue: Shoulder packed: down and away from your ear.
cues.why: A shrugged shoulder is less stable under a load held overhead.

cues.cue: Hips high in the bridge, glutes tight.
cues.why: Makes room for the leg sweep and trains hip extension.

cues.cue: Go slowly and pause at each stage.
cues.why: The value is control in every position, not speed.

breathing: Breathe out as you move into each new stage, breathe in during the short pause.

tempo.note: About 8-12 seconds up and the same down, pausing at each stage.

mistakes.name: Weight arm bends
mistakes.looks: The elbow softens and the weight sinks toward the face.
mistakes.fix: Lock the elbow; use a lighter weight or a shoe on the fist.
mistakes.why: Load shifts to the elbow and the weight can fall.

mistakes.name: Arm drifts off vertical
mistakes.looks: The weight leans forward or back instead of straight up.
mistakes.fix: Keep the knuckles to the ceiling, eyes on the weight.
mistakes.why: The further the weight drifts, the bigger the strain on the shoulder.

mistakes.name: Low bridge
mistakes.looks: The hips sag while the leg sweeps under.
mistakes.fix: Squeeze glutes and push the floor with the planted foot and hand.
mistakes.why: There is no room for the knee to pass and the lower back rounds.

mistakes.name: Shoulder shrugs up
mistakes.looks: The top shoulder rises to the ear.
mistakes.fix: Pull the shoulder down into its socket.
mistakes.why: The shoulder loses its stable base.

safety: Learn it with no weight (a shoe balanced on the fist), then a light bell.
Shoulder pain or poor overhead range: train the half get-up (to the hand) first.
Drop the weight to the side, never over yourself, if you lose control.

variants.change: Up to sitting on the hand or the high bridge, then back down.
Roll to the elbow and press up to the hand only.
Kettlebell held bell-up; grip and shoulder stability work much harder.
From the bridge, sweep into a low squat and stand, instead of the kneeling lunge.
No weight: hands behind the head; a kneel-to-stand pattern.

motion.basis: Stage order from ace2015 and the seven-stage description in shoulder-tgu2019. Joint angles are estimates of each stage position; trunk is measured from vertical so the lying stages are negative. Up phase only; the rig reverses the keyframes for the way down. Roll and trunk twist toward the posting hand are estimates.

sources.cite: A descriptive analysis of shoulder muscle activities during individual stages of the Turkish Get-Up exercise. J Bodyw Mov Ther. 2019 (PMID 30691756).
